paper_metadata.title: Simulation of a Variational Quantum Perceptron using Grover’s Algorithm

summary: The paper simulates two 2‑qubit quantum classifiers on the Iris dataset: a variational quantum perceptron (QVP) and a QVP augmented with a Grover amplitude‑amplification circuit. On an IBM QASM simulator, QVP reaches 0.90 validation accuracy after 100 iterations, while the Grover‑augmented model reaches 0.99, compared with 0.96 for a classical perceptron baseline. All experiments are simulator-based with no resource scaling or runtime analysis.

experiments.description: Variational quantum perceptron (QVP) trained and evaluated on the Iris dataset using a gate-based variational circuit on IBM QASM simulator.

notes: The paper explicitly states the QVP was evaluated using the ibmq qasm simulator.
The exact circuit depth, gate counts, and number of trainable parameters are not reported in the text provided.
Grover is not part of this experiment; it is a separate experiment below.
Table I shows classical perceptron validation accuracy of 0.96 while QVP reaches only 0.90 at 100 iterations.
Although the paper suggests quantum models may be more efficient, the reported metrics show the classical baseline outperforming the QVP model.

notes: The paper explicitly states the QVP-Grover model was run on the ibmq qasm simulator.
The Grover circuit is described qualitatively (Hadamard, CNOT, CZ, X), but no gate counts or depth are reported.
The reported loss value is approximate from the discussion (≈0.4).
Authors claim the QVP‑Grover model is more efficient and achieves higher validation accuracy (0.99 vs 0.96 for the classical perceptron) in Table I.
However the experiment uses a tiny 2‑qubit simulation on the Iris dataset with no runtime or scaling analysis, so practical advantage is not demonstrated.
